evaluation_rationale_and_hypothesis: Rationale: Tests how effectively a model recovers accuracy after massive, unforecasted anomalies. Hypothesis: The Dynamic Two-Stage Hybrid Model will prove superior due to real-time exogenous checkpoint floor error feedback corrections.
quantitative_metrics: Time-to-Recovery (TTR), Maximum Queue Deviation, Disruption Error Multipliers (R_RMSE, R_MASE)

evaluation_rationale_and_hypothesis: Rationale: Tests model accuracy under routine, everyday operational churn and minor schedule drift (10-15 minute delays). Hypothesis: Supervised Machine Learning models will excel at capturing routine baseline variance with zero feedback latency.
quantitative_metrics: Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE_routine), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE_routine)

evaluation_rationale_and_hypothesis: Rationale: Tests whether a model calibrated on one spatial layout (e.g., Terminal C at EWR) can accurately predict flow at another terminal (e.g., Terminal C at LGA) without extensive retraining. Hypothesis: Deterministic Flight Schedule baselines will generalize better than over-fitted decision trees memorizing localized terminal geometry.
quantitative_metrics: Cross-Validation Error Margins, Relative Transfer Ratio (RTR), Transfer MASE Percentage Change (Delta MASE)
